PREMARITAL AGREEMENT

This Premarital Agreement (this "Agreement") is made on February 14, 2026, between Rosalie Beaumont-Achterberg, residing at 88 Larkspur Terrace, Madison, Wisconsin ("Rosalie"), and Yusuf Demirci, residing at 412 North Blount Street, Madison, Wisconsin ("Yusuf"). Rosalie and Yusuf are each a "Party" and together the "Parties."

RECITALS

A. The Parties intend to marry on June 6, 2026, in Dane County, Wisconsin.

B. Each Party has property and financial obligations, and each has children or may have children from this or a prior relationship.

C. The Parties wish to define the rights each will have in the property of the other during the marriage, on the dissolution of the marriage, and at death, and to substitute the terms of this Agreement for the classification and division rules that would otherwise apply under Chapter 766 of the Wisconsin Statutes.

D. This Agreement is intended to be a marital property agreement under Wis. Stat. § 766.58 and a premarital agreement enforceable under Wisconsin law.

1. Effective Date.

This Agreement takes effect on the solemnization of the Parties' marriage. If the marriage does not occur, this Agreement is void and of no effect.

2. Disclosure.

Each Party has provided the other a written statement of assets, liabilities, and annual income, attached as Schedule A (Rosalie) and Schedule B (Yusuf). Each Party has read the other's statement, has had a reasonable opportunity to ask questions about it and to obtain further information, and acknowledges that the disclosure is fair and reasonable. Neither Party waives the right to disclosure; each acknowledges that disclosure has in fact been made.

3. Independent Counsel.

Rosalie is represented by Halvorsen & Nkemelu S.C. Yusuf is represented by Castellano Family Law LLC. Each Party has consulted independently with counsel of that Party's own choosing about the meaning and legal effect of this Agreement, has had adequate time to do so, and enters into this Agreement voluntarily and without coercion, duress, or undue influence. Neither Party's counsel represents the other Party.

4. Individual Property.

The property listed on a Party's schedule, together with all appreciation, income, rents, dividends, and proceeds of that property, and all property acquired by that Party by gift, devise, bequest, or inheritance at any time, is that Party's individual property and is not marital property. The classification is not changed by the use of marital funds or the personal effort of either Party to maintain or improve the property, and neither Party acquires any marital, community, or equitable interest in it, except as Section 6 provides for the residence.

5. Marital Property.

Property acquired during the marriage by either Party from earnings, other than property described in Section 4, is marital property owned equally by the Parties. Each Party's retirement plan contributions and accruals attributable to service during the marriage are marital property.

6. The Marital Residence.

If the Parties acquire a residence together during the marriage, it is marital property regardless of the source of the down payment, except that on dissolution each Party is first reimbursed, without interest, for individual property that Party contributed to the purchase, with the balance divided equally.

7. Debts.

Each Party's debts existing on the effective date remain that Party's separate obligation, and that Party shall indemnify and hold the other harmless from them, including reasonable attorneys' fees incurred in defending a claim. Debts incurred during the marriage for the Parties' joint living expenses are joint obligations. Neither Party may pledge the individual property of the other.

8. Spousal Support.

Neither Party waives the right to seek spousal support (maintenance) on dissolution. The Parties agree that maintenance, if any, is to be determined by the court under Wis. Stat. § 767.56 on the facts existing at the time, and that no term of this Agreement limits the court's authority to award it. The Parties acknowledge that a provision purporting to waive maintenance would be unenforceable to the extent it left a Party without reasonable support.

9. Children.

Nothing in this Agreement affects the right of any child to support, or the authority of a court to determine custody, physical placement, or child support. Any provision of this Agreement that is inconsistent with a child's right to support is void to that extent.

10. Estate Rights.

Except as this Agreement provides, each Party waives all rights in the estate of the other arising by reason of the marriage, including the elective share, homestead allowance, exempt property, family allowance, and the right to act as personal representative, and each shall on request execute any instrument necessary to give effect to this waiver. Nothing in this Section prevents a Party from making a gift or devise to the other, and this Agreement does not revoke any beneficiary designation.

11. Amendment and Revocation.

This Agreement may be amended or revoked only by a written agreement signed by both Parties. An amendment or revocation is enforceable without further consideration.

12. Enforcement, Governing Law, and Severability.

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Wisconsin. If any provision is held unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue in effect, except that if the property provisions of Sections 4 through 7 are held unenforceable as a whole, the entire Agreement is void. The Parties consent to the jurisdiction of the Circuit Court for Dane County, Wisconsin, in any proceeding concerning this Agreement.

13. Voluntary Execution.

Each Party has read this Agreement in full, understands its terms, has had the opportunity to review it with counsel over a period of not less than thirty days before signing, and signs it freely and voluntarily.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Agreement on the date first written above.

/s/ Rosalie Beaumont-Achterberg
Rosalie Beaumont-Achterberg

/s/ Yusuf Demirci
Yusuf Demirci
